solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Penny adrift, so pull a face

parts.note: something adrift is out, loose from its moorings

explanation.surface: A coin has floated away, so someone grimaces.
explanation.definitionFit: To pout is to push out the lips sulkily, a way of making a face.

clue.text: Strength and determination shown by English rock 'n' roll star

parts.note: steel means grit, firmness of resolve

explanation.surface: A British rock 'n' roll singer shows grit and resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Steele was an early British rock 'n' roll star of the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy Steele is a famous example of a British rock 'n' roll singer.

clue.text: Hand on knight, a chess piece

parts.note: a paw is a jocular word for a hand
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A player puts a hand on a knight while moving a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The humblest piece on the board, eight per side, is this one.

clue.text: Display shabby articles also

parts.note: tat is cheap, tasteless goods
too means also

explanation.surface: A show of worn-out goods as well.
explanation.walkthrough: A military TATTOO is an outdoor display of marching bands and drill, such as the Edinburgh Tattoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A military tattoo is a public display of drill and music by troops.

clue.text: Extremely small piece in paper's third column

indicators.note: third points to the third letter of the word paper

parts.note: a newspaper column is an article

explanation.surface: A tiny item tucked into a newspaper's third column.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a minute fragment or speck of matter.

clue.text: Go through mountains to reach area used for target practice

parts.note: to rifle is to search through, ransacking
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: Someone crosses the mountains to get to a shooting ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A firing range where rifles are shot at targets is this kind of place.

clue.text: Italian aristocrat not implicated in unseemly cases

indicators.note: implicated in means involved in, so the first word joins the pool of letters to be mixed
unseemly suggests things out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Italian noblewoman is cleared of involvement in some indecent cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' reads as part of the surface's denial, but it is fodder: 'implicated in' draws it into the letters that 'unseemly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A contessa is an Italian countess, a woman of noble rank.

clue.text: Aroma's very different in metal urn

indicators.note: different signals the letters are made into something else

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving the letters of aromas

explanation.surface: Tea smells quite unlike itself when brewed in a metal vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges AROMAS plus V (very) into the urn.
explanation.definitionFit: A samovar is a Russian metal urn used for heating water for tea.

clue.text: Article about spies in plant

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
ca, short for circa, means about
the CIA is the American intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece concerns secret agents hiding in a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Acacia is a genus of trees and shrubs, including wattle.

clue.text: Energy required to cross river current

indicators.note: required to cross says one word must straddle another, holding it inside

parts.note: steam is a source of power or energy

explanation.surface: Power is needed to get across a river's flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a flow of water, air or electricity, a current.

clue.text: Short memo to be written about volunteers, each one? Forget it!

indicators.note: short means cut down, losing a final letter

parts.note: a note is a brief memo

indicators.note: written about means one set of letters is put around another

parts.note: all means each one, every single one
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A brief memo is to be drafted about the volunteers, every one of them, then dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' docks the memo's final letter; 'to be written about' wraps one piece round the volunteers. The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are emphatic refusals or brush-offs, meaning no need, don't mention it.

clue.text: Overaction bars criminal from viewing vehicle

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hammy acting gets someone banned from a railway sightseeing carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: An observation car is a railway carriage with large windows for sightseeing.

clue.text: Complaint about food raised — something in a bun?

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or grievance

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read from the bottom up

parts.note: re means about or concerning
grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: A grumble about the food goes up: what's in this roll?
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns RE plus GRUB upwards, giving BURGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A patty of minced meat is usually served in a bread roll, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Major oil centre close to vast lake in America

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of the word vast
in places the lake letter inside the country

parts.note: USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A big oil hub sits near a huge lake in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa in Oklahoma was once called the Oil Capital of the World.

clue.text: Catch that woman palming ace

indicators.note: palming means holding in the hand, so one piece is concealed inside another

parts.note: her refers to that woman
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: Spot a female cardsharp hiding an ace in her hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch what someone says is to hear it.

clue.text: Two-wheeler in red (was green?)

indicators.note: in puts the bicycle inside the colour word

parts.note: taken as written
a cycle is a bicycle

explanation.surface: A bike painted red, or was it green?
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' here means environmentally friendly, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reprocessed for reuse has been treated in an eco-friendly way, hence green with a question mark.

clue.text: Sappers left in charge of historical object

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers, are abbreviated RE
IC means in charge

explanation.surface: Army engineers left in charge of an ancient artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object surviving from an earlier time.

clue.text: Rhythm of dance organised in outskirts of Carlisle

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the outer pair
outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters of the city name
organised means arranged, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: The beat of a dance put on at the edge of a Cumbrian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges the dance; 'in' sets that inside the city's edge letters. Carlisle is a city in north-west England, near the Scottish border.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadence is the rhythmic rise and fall of sound or movement.

clue.text: Greek leaving Scottish village for high peak

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so letters drop out of the word

parts.note: Gretna is a village on the Scottish border, famed for runaway weddings

explanation.surface: A Greek departs a Scottish village for a lofty summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna in Sicily is a tall volcanic mountain, a high peak.

clue.text: The tips I give cabbies may not be well received

definitions.text: The tips I give cabbies may not be well received

parts.words: The tips I give cabbies may not be well received
parts.note: the tips are not money but unwanted directions offered from behind to the driver of a taxi

explanation.surface: A passenger worries that drivers won't appreciate the gratuities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips' looks like gratuities but means advice on driving, given by a passenger behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger who keeps giving the driver unwanted advice is described by this idiom.

clue.text: Splendid salesman aboard coach going north

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means read upwards
aboard means on a vehicle, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a coach is a bus
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A splendid salesman is riding a coach heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' puts the salesman inside the coach, and 'going north' turns the whole of that upwards, not just the coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb is a synonym of splendid, magnificent, excellent.

clue.text: At home and not at home, to some extent

parts.note: in means at home
away means absent, not at home

explanation.surface: Being both in and out at once, partly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning partly, in some respects.

clue.text: Crazy shot gaining trophy

parts.note: a crack is an attempt, a shot
a pot is slang for a cup or trophy

explanation.surface: A wild shot wins a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackpot as an adjective means eccentric, mad.

clue.text: Extremely large implement

parts.note: too means excessively, extremely

explanation.surface: A very big piece of equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool is an implement used for work.

clue.text: Subtle difference in tone used by sister describing a church

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing round means one piece encloses another

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A nun's description of a church relies on fine shades of meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' means tracing round, so NUN wraps A.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a slight shade of difference in meaning, colour or tone.

clue.text: Not windy in local market

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the phrase local market

explanation.surface: A still day at the neighbourhood market.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm weather is still, without wind.

clue.text: Never worried about eastern front

indicators.note: about means going round, so the scrambled letters surround the other
worried means disturbed, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: Someone is never anxious about the eastern battlefront.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges NEVER to VENER, and 'about' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin outer layer, a superficial front or facade.

clue.text: Boiler suit complete with latest in wellingtons

parts.note: overall means total, complete

indicators.note: latest means last, so the final letter of wellingtons

explanation.surface: A full set of workwear, with wellies to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Wellingtons are rubber boots, so the surface is a work outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Overalls are a one-piece protective garment, a boiler suit.
